problem: Is the function $g(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}+x{y}^{2}+5{z}^{2}$ homogeneous? If so, what is its degree?
worked_solution:
A function $g(x,y,z)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
g(tx,ty,tz)={t}^{n}g(x,y,z).
$$

So first, we compute $g(tx,ty,tz),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}g(x,y,z)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(tx,ty,tz) & =2(tx)^{2}+(tx)(ty)^{2}+5(tz)^{2} \\  & =2{t}^{2}{x}^{2}+{t}^{3}x{y}^{2}+5{t}^{2}{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

It's impossible to write this as

$$
{t}^{n}g(x,y,z)={t}^{n}(2{x}^{2}+x{y}^{2}+5{z}^{2})
$$

and so $g(x,y,z)$ is not homogeneous.
